'''''Silene pendula''''', called the '''nodding catchfly''' or '''drooping catchfly''', is a species of flowering plant in the genus ''[[Silene]]'', native to Italy, Greece, and Turkey, and introduced to scattered locations in North America, South America, Africa, Europe and Asia.<ref name="158042-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:158042-1 |title=''Silene pendula'' L. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=13 February 2021 }}</ref> A number of cultivars are available.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Silene pendula'' nodding catchfly |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/113616/Silene-pendula/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |accessdate=13 February 2021 |quote=Other common names; ... Italian catchfly, pendulous catchfly }}</ref> A 2020 study showed with certainty that, despite their morphological similarities, ''[[Silene cisplatensis]]'' is not synonymous with ''Silene pendula''.<ref name="1_of_560_Google_Scholar_Hits" >{{cite journal |title=A new taxonomic backbone for the infrageneric classification of the species-rich genus ''Silene'' (Caryophyllaceae) |year=2020 |last1=Jafari |first1=Farzaneh |last2=Zarre |first2=Shahin |last3=Gholipour |first3=Abbas |last4=Eggens |first4=Frida |last5=Rabeler |first5=Richard K. |last6=Oxelman |first6=Bengt |journal=Taxon |volume=69 |issue=2 |pages=337–368 |doi=10.1002/tax.12230 |bibcode=2020Taxon..69..337J |hdl=2027.42/156144 |s2cid=225737766 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
